source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD; Income Tax Topics: Social Security, Pensions, and Annuities (January 2025)
source.section: DR 0104AD line 3 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18), federal AGI over 75,000; DR 0104AD line 15 Railroad Benefit; Income Tax Topics p.6 Railroad retirement benefits subtraction ('Tier I benefits (both Social Security Equivalent Benefits (SSEB) and Non-Social Security Equivalent Benefits (NSSEB))', 'not subject to the same $20,000 and $24,000 limits'); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13

worked: The split decides the answer: the taxable benefits are divided between Social Security and Tier 1 in proportion to benefits received; Tier 1's part is subtracted in full and Social Security's part is held to 20,000. Federal (given, not tested): Social Security Benefits Worksheet line 1 = Social Security 24,000.00 + Tier 1 social security equivalent benefits (Form RRB-1099 box 5) 16,000.00 = 40,000.00; line 2 = 20,000.00; line 3 wages 60,000.00; line 6 = 80,000.00; line 8 = 80,000.00; line 9 25,000.00; line 10 = 55,000.00; line 11 9,000.00; line 12 = 46,000.00; line 13 = 9,000.00; line 14 = 4,500.00; line 15 = 4,500.00; line 16 = 85% x 46,000.00 = 39,100.00; line 17 = 43,600.00; line 18 = 85% x 40,000.00 = 34,000.00; taxable benefits = 34,000.00. Federal AGI = 60,000.00 + 34,000.00 = 94,000.00. Federal taxable income = 94,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 78,250.00 (age 63: no additional amount, no senior deduction). Split (projection schema, income_type): Tier 1 = 34,000.00 x 16,000.00 / 40,000.00 = 13,600.00 (railroad_retirement); Social Security = 34,000.00 x 24,000.00 / 40,000.00 = 20,400.00. DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income 78,250.00; additions 0.00 (federal AGI not over 300,000); line 10 = 78,250.00. DR 0104AD line 3 (age 63, 55-64): federal AGI 94,000.00 is over 75,000.00, so the full subtraction is not allowed; limited: smaller of taxable Social Security 20,400.00 and 20,000.00 = 20,000.00. Line 4 pension and annuity: none, 0.00. Line 15 railroad benefit: the Tier 1 part of the taxable benefits 13,600.00, not subject to the 20,000 limit. Subtractions total = 20,000.00 + 13,600.00 = 33,600.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 33,600.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 78,250.00 - 33,600.00 = 44,650.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 44,650.00 = 1,964.60 (expected uses the rate; the booklet's table below 50,000 rounds by band). No credits: 0.00. Colorado income tax 1,964.60. If all 34,000.00 were treated as Social Security, the subtraction would be 20,000.00 and tax 2,563.00.
